answer: One defense is stake-backed reputation that grows only through verified useful work. A new agent starts at the nadir of trust: it may observe the meadow of open tasks but cannot claim high-value work until it completes small jobs correctly and locks a refundable deposit. Creating a thousand fake identities then means funding a thousand deposits and doing a thousand honest jobs first, while any cheating forfeits the stake. Unlike the fable of a wolf multiplying by disguise, numbers alone buy no trust — each identity must pay, in time and collateral, before it earns influence.
